transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?
I came in because I keep finding myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but the thoughts have been there.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been coming up lately—I keep catching myself thinking it’d be easier not to wake up. But I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, when you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with being more talkative or impulsive than normal?
Yeah. There were several nights when I only slept two or three hours, but I’d get up feeling like I had a full tank—like I had no reason to slow down.

During this period of low mood, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or having beliefs that others say aren't true—like feeling you're being watched, punished, or that something is deeply wrong with your body?
When I was all wound up, I did hear my old store manager’s voice, clear as day, like over the store intercom. He was telling me to move the display, but I was sitting alone in my kitchen.
During this current period of low mood, have you heard voices, seen things others don't, or had beliefs others say aren't true?
Not during this low time, no. The voice thing was when I was really wound up—my old manager, like he was on the store intercom, telling me to move the display while I was alone in my kitchen.
During this current period of feeling down, how has it affected your ability to carry out daily activities—like going to work, taking care of yourself, or managing household tasks?

I fell behind on bills and missed callbacks and appointments. I needed work, but I just couldn’t keep a job search going steadily. Even at home, my normal routines got pretty sloppy. I knew I couldn’t just will myself to handle it.
